text:
Mark Stone has ten goals in 18 games for Vegas, and that number comes with a warning label. He is shooting 29 percent (22 last season, already high) on chances worth 6.5 goals, and the Golden Knights have scored 9.6 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Three of those goals came in one night against Calgary on October 15. Expect the scoring pace to slow.

What it will not take away is why Vegas leans on its captain. Evolving-Hockey rated him third among 401 forwards last season at 4.1 wins above replacement, and unlike most high scorers he took chances away: opponents got 0.17 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there (94th percentile). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.6 primary shot assists per 60, 96th percentile. A sixth-round pick in 2010 who grew into a Stanley Cup captain does a lot of things.

He is playing 18:37 a night, slightly less lately, and our projection puts him around 88 points if he plays the rest of the way. Watch the shot totals: 35 in 18 games is a low number for a ten-goal player.
headline: Stone at 34: the finishing will fade, the rest won't
